citation: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, Storm Events Database, 2014-2026. U.S. government work, public domain. https://www.ncdc.noaa.gov/stormevents/

events.title: Heavy Rain near Riverton
events.description: 2 deaths (indirect). El Dorado County. Broadcast Media relayed information from California Highway Patrol regarding an accident that occurred on May 26th around 4 PM PDT. Showers and thunderstorms brought wet road conditions on May 26th to Highway 50 in El Dorado County. Just east of Ice House Road, a vehicle veered off the roadway and into the American River. Rainfall amounts of 0.15-0.25 were observed at the time of the incident. A 35 year old woman died at the scene, and a 5 year old boy died in the hospital as a result of the accident. An 11 year old boy and a 41 year old man were injured from this accident.

events.title: Flood near Paicines
events.description: 1 death. San Benito County. A small sedan attempted to ford Tres Pinos Creek along Browns Valley Road near Paicines on the night of February 17, with first responders responding to the scene during the night. The next morning, the driver was found walking along Highway 25 asking about the location of the passenger. The passenger's body was eventually found a mile downstream of where the car had gotten stranded. The driver was later arrested on charges of gross vehicular manslaughter. At the time of the incident, the TESC1 river gauge on Tres Pinos Creek measured stages above 2 feet, compared to a typical stage of less…

events.title: Flash Flood near Goleta
events.description: 1 death. Santa Barbara County. Heavy rainfall generated flash flooding from Maria Ygnacio Creek. One man was swept down the creek and drowned. His body was found in the creek near the intersection of San Marcos Road and Via Parva.

events.title: Heavy Rain near Clipper Gap
events.description: 1 death. Placer County. There were numerous reports of roadway flooding and rises on small creeks and streams in the area due to heavy rain. A hiker went missing on January 2nd around 2:00 PM. Search and research operations from Placer County to help find the missing individual where underway through the weekend. The hiker's body was recovered Monday afternoon.

events.title: Flood near Williams
events.description: 1 death. Colusa County. Around 3 PM PST on December 26th, a vehicle hydroplaned and crashed on Interstate 5 in Williams, CA in heavy rain. Initially there were 2 minor injuries and 2 critical injuries, but later one of the critical injuries was updated to a fatality.

events.title: Flood near Pt Pleasant
events.description: 1 death. Sacramento County. California Highway Patrol reported a weather related fatality event with an SUV crashing into a power pole on Franklin Boulevard due to wet roads.

events.title: Flash Flood near Redding
events.description: 1 death. Shasta County. A Convergence Zone set up over Redding/Shasta County around 1 PM on Sunday, December 21. Heavy rain fell until around 7 PM, where there was a lull before another line redeveloped and brought additional moderate to heavy rain into the late evening. County officials reported numerous reports of widespread flash flooding, stranded vehicles, and road closures. Commercial and residential damage was reported to over 170 structures with preliminary damage estimates upwards of 7 million dollars, from both public and private. One fatality was reported. Rain estimates were around 3-7 in 9 hours over…

events.title: Flood near Pleasant Grove
events.description: 1 death. Sutter County. California Highway Patrol reported that a 71 year old man drowned after his car was swept into a creek crossing as a bridge flooded on Fifield Road in Pleasant Grove in Sutter County due to heavy rain.

events.title: Flash Flood near Lenwood
events.description: 1 death. San Bernardino County. Flash flooding on Main Street between Lenwood Road and Sweeten Lane swept away a car, killing a two-year old boy and injuring his father.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Fallen Leaf
events.description: 8 deaths. El Dorado County. Buoy data on Lake Tahoe indicated a northerly wind gust of 45 mph from nearby showers and collapsing thunderstorms. This caused significant waves on Lake Tahoe, with multiple boats damaged and one boat capsized near Emerald Bay, causing 8 fatalities out of the 10 on board. The two that survived were wearing life jackets, while the other 8 did not.

events.title: Flood near Carmel Vly
events.description: 1 death. Monterey County. An elderly man went missing while walking his dog in Garland Ranch Regional Park, and was last heard from around 10:30 AM. Around 11 AM, hikers found his dog and returned it to the man's family, who reported him missing at noon. Monterey County park rangers were assisted by local and state resources in a swift-water search, who ultimately found the man's body in Carmel River.

events.title: Flood near Molino
events.description: 1 death. Sonoma County. A man was found dead around 7 a.m. On February 6th at Sanford and Hall roads, a rural stretch west of Santa Rosa lined with scattered homes and open fields. Sheriffï¿½ï¿½ï¿½s deputies had been searching for an 83-year-old man reported missing around 9 p.m. on the 5th. Investigators have not yet confirmed whether the recovered body is his.

events.title: Flood near Mark West Spgs
events.description: 1 death. Sonoma County. A man was found dead wedged inside a culvert around 4:40 p.m. on February 5 on Franz Valley Road, a narrow, winding route through steep hills northeast of Santa Rosa.

events.title: Flood near Auburn
events.description: 2 deaths. Placer County. Placer County Sheriff reported a group of three men went to fish in the North American River, north of Folsom Lake on November 23rd. Two of the men, both 20 years old, got into the water. One of them was swept away by the strong currents and the second man tried to help but was also pulled into the current. The recovery operation was extremely technical and in a portion of the river with rapids and strong current due to the storm. Both 20 year old men drowned and their bodies were recovered downstream on November 25th.

events.title: Flood near Guerneville
events.description: 1 death. Sonoma County. A 911 caller reported to Sonoma County dispatch that they had seen a car go into floodwaters near Mays Canyon Road and Highway 116. Rescue crews arrived and found the vehicle, and the driver was found dead.

events.title: Dust Devil near Ellis
events.description: 2 deaths. Riverside County. Media outlets from LA reported 2 fatalities associated with skydiving deaths. At least 1 large dust devil was reported at the time of the accident and was reported to cause the instructor to loose control of the chute. The temperature was 103F and wind gusts were as high as 18 mph at nearby weather stations. This region is flat and know as the Inland Empire. The skydiving facility is at the Perris Valley airport. The instructor and the student died on scene and the hospital. Both skydivers were reported to be female and 28 years old.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Yosemite Natl Park
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Mariposa County. Media report of a 20 year old hiker slipping and falling off of cables while descending Half Dome during a thunderstorm which was producing heavy rainfall and gusty winds. The fall resulted in fatal injuries.

events.title: Debris Flow near Summit City
events.description: 2 deaths. Shasta County. At approximately 9:00 AM PST on Thursday, February, 22, 2024, Shasta County Sheriff's Office responded to a report that rocks and debris had broken away from a hillside, near a drainage culvert that leads to the Sacramento River. Two juveniles were caught in the debris, fell down the hillside and died. Heavy rainfall impacted the area from February 18-21, 2024, with observed rainfall totals of 3-8 inches near the site of the incident.

events.title: Flood near Lincoln Muni Arpt
events.description: 1 death. Placer County. California Highway Patrol and Placer County OES reported a fatality of a driver that drove through standing water on a flooded road, lost control, and flipped the vehicle, coming to a rest in standing water on Nicolaus Road near Marcum Road.

events.title: Flood near Tulare Airpark
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Tulare County. A truck slid off of SR 99 and crashed into a divider near the exchange with Ave 200. The driver of the truck was killed in the accident. A flood watch was in effect for Tulare at the time of the accident and rain was ongoing as well.

events.title: Flood near San Ysidro
events.description: 1 death. San Diego County. A 61 year old man drowned in the Tijuana River Channel on February 6 while attempting to cross the international border, following heavy rain in San Diego. San Diego Fire-Rescue swift water crews pulled the body from the river and despite attempted lifesaving measures, the man was pronounced dead at the scene.

events.title: Flash Flood near (see)san Diego Gille
events.description: 2 deaths. San Diego County. Fox5 in San Diego reported that two people, 46 year old female and 48 year old male, were found deceased, drowning in a creek in Santee, near the intersection of Prospect Avenue and Cuyamaca Road. Exactly how and when the deceased were swept into the creek is unknown.

events.title: Heavy Rain near Ignacio
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Marin County. A man drove off a slick Highway 101 North in Novato just after 5 PM on January 20, and wrapped his car around the traffic light on the frontage road, north of Hamilton Parkway, outside Safeway. According to the California Highway Patrol, speed and wet roadway were factors. The Novato Fire Department extracted the man from the wreckage and paramedics tried, unsuccessfully, to perform CPR. The man was taken to a hospital, where he died of his injuries. The car was totaled and a fence and light pole were damaged. Report courtesy KTVU television (FOX San Francisco-Oakland).

events.title: Flood near Sanger Wndr Vly Arpt
events.description: 2 deaths. Fresno County. Fresno, Kings and Tulare County Emergency Managers reported flooding along the Kings River downstream from Pine Flat Dam as a result of increased releases prompted by increased runoff from snow melt. Two young children who were swimming in the river with their mother on May 21 were swept away by the fast moving waters and were found dead shortly afterward. Neither child was wearing a life vest.

events.title: Flood near Elmhurst
events.description: 1 death. Alameda County. The roof of a warehouse on 650 85th Ave in Oakland collapsed at 3:20 AM. A 57-year old man was struck by falling debris and died; a woman suffered a broken nose. KTVU television reported that city inspectors found that water had been ponding on the roof and drains were not properly cleaned.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Crissy Aaf
events.description: 1 death. San Francisco County. A jogger near the intersection of JFK Drive and 30th Avenue within the Golden Gate Park noticed a woman down next to a fallen tree branch. Firefighters arrived to provide life-saving measures, but said that the victim had died. At the time of the incident, a Special Weather Statement was valid for the area, with wind gusts up to 40 mph and pea sized hail possible.

events.title: Flood near Goshen
events.description: 2 deaths (indirect). Tulare County. The Tulare County Emergency Manager reported that flooding from heavy rainfall resulted in a large eucalyptus tree falling on northbound SR 99 causing a multi-car chain reaction crash at the intersection of SR 99 and Betty Dr. in Goshen which caused one fatality. The fallen tree also killed an individual who was riding a motorcycle and hit the tree.

events.title: Flood near Mirabell Park
events.description: 1 death. Sonoma County. Roadway flooding was reported along Mark West Creek near the communities of Forestville and Trenton. A 43-year old woman from Ukiah was recovered on the 10th after her car got stuck in floodwaters. She had called 911 to report that her car was taking on water on Trenton-Healdsburg Road. The call cut out, and Sonoma County Fire sent swift water rescue gear around 10:10 AM on the 9th. A helicopter from the Sonoma County Sheriff's office was also involved. The search was called off at sunset, and by the morning of the 10th, the vehicle was found sitting in 8 to 10 feet of floodwaters.

events.title: Flash Flood near Avila Beach
events.description: 1 death. San Luis Obispo County. A 60 year old woman was swept away in her SUV by raging flood waters along Avila Beach Road.

events.title: Flash Flood near Wellsona
events.description: 1 death. San Luis Obispo County. A woman and her 5 year old child were swept down a flooded roadway near San Marcos Creek. The woman survived, but her 5 year old child died.

events.title: Flood near Vacaville Jct
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Solano County. A woman died in a crash likely caused by speed and standing water in Fairfield on Vanden Road at One Lake. Investigators said the roadway was partially flooded due to rain from the recent downpours. Police said the woman was heading eastbound on the road when she came across a patch of standing water and hydroplaned before losing control of the vehicle and crashing into a utility pole.

events.title: Flood near Coloma
events.description: 1 death (indirect). El Dorado County. On January 3 in El Dorado County, a 33 year-old male drowned in the South Fork of the American River near Coloma, CA. It is unknown how he ended up in the river.

events.title: Flash Flood near Slough House
events.description: 1 death. Sacramento County. There was a male fatality due to drowning in a submerged car, confirmed by Cosumnes Fire Department near SR 99 and Dillard Rd. A levee breech on the Cosumnes River caused the flash flood. This was one of three drowning deaths reported from the flash flood event. The Cosumnes Fire Department said they rescued dozens of people in the area over the past 24 hours. A helicopter from Metro Fire also rescued several people in the area. SR 99 remained closed due to flooding on the roadway. Several vehicles are still stuck in the flood waters. Wilton firefighters responded to 25 vehicles stranded in…

events.title: Flash Flood near Mc Connell
events.description: 1 death. Sacramento County. The California Highway Patrol on January 4 reported a fatality associated with the December 31 - January 1 flash flood due to levee breaks. A female body was found outside a vehicle near Dillard Road east of CA-99. This is one of three confirmed fatalities from this event.

events.title: Flash Flood near Twin Cities
events.description: 1 death. Sacramento County. Sacramento County Sheriff confirmed a drowning on January 4 associated with the December 31 - January 1 flash flood event. A female body was found inside a vehicle. This was the third drowning associated with the event. This flooding was due to levee breaks on the Cosumnes River.

events.title: Flood near Wayne
events.description: 1 death. Santa Clara County. A 56-year old man was found drowned in fast moving water on January 1 in Upper Penitencia Creek in San Jose after the creek overflowed the previous night.

events.title: Debris Flow near Foresta
events.description: 2 deaths. Mariposa County. Yosemite National Park employees reported two people were killed by a rockslide near the intersection of SR 140 and Big Oak Flat Road in Yosemite National Park.

events.title: Flash Flood near Ontario
events.description: 3 deaths. San Bernardino County. Ontario Fire department reported 6 person in the swiftwater channel in John Galvin park where the channel begins near I-10. Rainfall rates of 0.50 to 0.75 inches per hour had occurred from 7 am to 9 am in Ontario and Rancho Cucamonga. 3 persons were rescued. 3 more person were later found drowned in a retaining pond which was filled 15 to 20 feet high with storm runoff water. The bodies were not found until several days later due the water being too deep and low visibility. Multiple agencies were involved in the week long recovery efforts. The channel runs south past Ontario airport to where…

events.title: Debris Flow near Forest Falls
events.description: 1 death. San Bernardino County. Heavy thunderstorms associated with remnant moisture from post-tropical cyclone Kay produced torrential rain over the Apple and El Dorado burn scars on the afternoon of September 12. Multiple debris flows occurred following torrential one-hour rainfall rates exceeding debris flow guidance from the USGS and CAGS. Two of the debris flows traveled several miles including the Banning Canyon wash showing debris logs and ash water. The most impactful debris flow occurred in Forest Falls and Oak Glen, where the flow traveled at least 3 miles down Oakland Road with 4 foot boulders, logs over-topping…

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Havasu Lake
events.description: 1 death. San Bernardino County. Waves estimated to be six feet high swept across Lake Havasu due to severe thunderstorm winds. Multiple boaters in distress were rescued from their crafts and from the water. One person was trapped under a capsized craft near the Havasu Landing Casino and drowned.

events.title: Lightning near South Whittier
events.description: 1 death. Los Angeles County. In the community of Pico Rivera, a woman was struck and killed by a bolt of lightning.

events.title: Flash Flood near Palo Verde
events.description: 2 deaths. Imperial County. Very heavy rainfall occurred along SR 78 in northeast Imperial County with amounts estimated to be approaching 7 inches in some places. This resulted in considerable flooding along the highway. The California Highway Patrol reported that a vehicle was swept off SR 78 at Milpitas Wash before overturning in the wash. Both occupants perished in the flash flood.

events.title: Lightning near Mono Hot Spgs
events.description: 1 death. Fresno County. The Fresno County Sherrifs Office reported a 37 year old male hiker on the John Muir Trail near Muir Trail Ranch was struck by lightning and killed during a thunderstorm around 200 pm PDT on July 30.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Havasu Lake
events.description: 1 death (indirect). San Bernardino County. A man drowned on the California side of Lake Havasu. Thunderstorm winds gusting to 46 mph contributed to the drowning.

events.title: Flash Flood near San Ysidro
events.description: 1 death. San Diego County. San Diego fire department and rescue and U.S. Border Patrol report 8 people trapped in a flooding storm drain between Otay Mesa and San Ysidro. 7 people were helped to safety with one fatality.

events.title: Lightning near Sierraville Drwtr Ar
events.description: 1 death. Sierra County. A 47-year-old Nevada man died after being struck by lightning while on a jet ski at Stampede Reservoir in Sierra County on Saturday 25 July. His body went underwater near the boat ramp and divers later found his body 20 yards from the shoreline. The lightning also struck the man's son, who was knocked unconscious and was severely burned according to an eyewitness.

events.title: Flood near (see)san Diego Gille
events.description: 1 death (indirect). San Diego County. Between 6pm and 8pm on March 10th, heavy rain in El Cajon and Santee was observed. A vehicle was traveling on I-8 westbound when it crashed into the Forrester Creek canal near First street and Naranca Avenue in El Cajon. As they were trying to escape, one of the passengers got caught in the fast-moving canal (but still within its banks) and was swept miles away. The person was located about 5 miles down Forrester creek near Prospect Avenue in Santee. When pulled from the water, the individual was alive but unconscious, but was later pronounced dead at the hospital.

events.title: Heavy Rain near Herndon
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Fresno County. Moderate to heavy rain caused a multiple vehicle accident on SR 99 just north of Fresno. Some of the individuals who had occupied the cars in the crash were then struck by a drunk driver which killed one of the individuals.

events.title: Hail near Miranda
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Humboldt County. One person killed and others injured when driver lost control of vehicle while driving across small hail accumulation on highway.

events.title: Flood near Arlynda Corners
events.description: 1 death. Humboldt County. Thirty-five year old man drowned attempting to reach his home while crossing floodwaters from the Eel River. Water was reported to be 4 to 5 feet deep and fast moving.

events.title: Debris Flow near San Francisco
events.description: 1 death (indirect). San Francisco County. Cliff collapsed on two women and a dog at Fort Funston near San Francisco. The steep cliffs are prone to landslides, but previous rainfall may have contributed, one woman did not survive https://www.sfgate.com/news/article/fort-funston-Kyra-Sunshine-Scarlet-13720685.php.

events.title: Flash Flood near Joshua Tree Arpt
events.description: 1 death. San Bernardino County. Numerous roads and intersections were flooded in Yucca Valley and Joshua Tree, at least four homes were flooded, at least four vehicles were stranded, and at least six swift water rescues occurred. One man was killed when his vehicle was swept away by flood waters.

events.title: Heavy Rain near Schellville
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Sonoma County. A fatal car crash occurred during heavy rain on Highway 121 near Napa Road https://www.pressdemocrat.com/news/9179304-181/fatal-sonoma-crash-in-heavy.

events.title: Flood near Roseland
events.description: 1 death. Sonoma County. Santa Rosa Fire Department reported that a body was found in Santa Rosa Creek west of the Pierson St Bridge https://patch.com/california/sonomavalley/body-recovered-santa-rosa-creek.

events.title: Flash Flood near Mortmar
events.description: 1 death. Riverside County. Thunderstorms with very heavy rain developed across portions of eastern Riverside County during the evening hours on September 30th. The stronger storms produced intense rain that led to flash flooding to the southwest of Joshua Tree National Park and to the north of the Salton Sea. At 1925PST (2025 PDT) the California Highway Patrol reported that Box Canyon Road was closed at the Mecca Copia Trail due to flash flooding. Significant impacts were reported to have occurred further downstream. Major damage was reportedly done to the Box Canyon Road forcing the road to be closed for days. It was…

events.title: Heavy Rain near Yosemite Natl Park
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Mariposa County. Report on Twitter that a hiker on the cables of Half Dome in Yosemite National Park slipped and fell off of the cables during a thunderstorm. The hiker was found dead from the fall the next day after a search and rescue was performed.

events.title: Flash Flood near Coulterville
events.description: 2 deaths. Mariposa County. Mariposa Office of Emergency Services reported several homes flooded and roadways washed out. While many roadways were washed out across Northwestern Mariposa County, the homes were generally impacted near Lake Don Pedro, Hornitos, and the City of Mariposa. The two fatalities that did occur in the area were both related to a person driving into a flooded roadway. One was along highway 132 west of Coulterville and the other was near Cathey's Valley where a 72 year old woman was found dead nearly four months later.

events.title: Debris Flow near Summerland
events.description: 21 deaths. Santa Barbara County. Intense rainfall generated a large and deadly mud and debris flow in the community of Montecito, around the burn scar of the Thomas fire. Automated rain gauges in the area indicated very intense rainfall, reaching as high as 0.54 inches in 5 minutes. The intense rainfall resulted in a mud and debris estimated to be 15 feet high. This event resulted in the confirmed deaths of 21 residents (2 missing) as well as destroying 128 residences and damaging 307 others. Highway 101 was closed for days due to the mud and debris.

events.title: Flood near Jelly
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Tehama County. Two men and a woman were trying to get to their home in a flooded area via a canoe but it tipped in the process, deputies said. Tehama County Sheriff's Boating Safety crews responded and rescued one man and a woman, however, the other man drowned.

events.title: Flood near Wyo
events.description: 1 death. Glenn County. A 45-year-old woman drowned after driving around road closures on County Road FF, and into floodwaters northwest of the town of Orland. The drowning was reported about 9:05 a.m. on the rural county road, which is prone to flooding. The woman's SUV was swept down Hambright Creek. When rescue teams responded, the water was so deep there was no sign of a vehicle, and a dive team was necessary for the recovery.

events.title: Flash Flood near Victorville
events.description: 1 death. San Bernardino County. Three vehicles swept from Rodeo Dr. near Pebble Beach Park. Swift water rescues were conducted to rescue 3 people. One fatality was reported.

events.title: Flash Flood near Rainbow
events.description: 2 deaths. San Diego County. A swift water rescue team pulled a man from a submerged car in a small creek near Old Highway 395 and 5th St. in Rainbow. A young boy, also in the car, was swept down stream before rescuers arrived. The boys body was recovered on the 26th.

events.title: Heavy Rain near Fallbrook
events.description: 1 death (indirect). San Diego County. An 80 ft oak tree fell on a mini van killing the driver. Saturated soils were likely an influencing factor. Winds were light at the time.

events.title: Heavy Rain near (fch) Chandler Af
events.description: 1 death (indirect). Fresno County. Moderate to heavy rain in Fresno on Highway 99 north of Highway 41 interchange may have contributed to a fatal car crash around 1900 PST. The stretch of highway 99 was closed until around midnight 11/21 due to the crash investigation.

events.title: Thunderstorm Wind near Pacific Beach
events.description: 1 death. San Diego County. A pine tree 8 ft in diameter succumbed to strong winds, falling on 4 cars and killing a 48 year old woman who was driving down Ingraham Street. An additional tree fell during the cleanup operations, injuring 2 reporters.

events.title: Flash Flood near Forest Falls
events.description: 1 death. San Bernardino County. A flash flood at Mill Creek crossing...40 feet wide and 8 to 12 inches deep. The head of the flash flood was 3 to 4 feet deep. From Victor Valley news group: flood waters overtook a couple hiking. An off-duty sheriff's deputy heard the couple calling for help and was able to save the young woman, but the man was swept away. The body of the victim, a Rancho Cucamonga man in his 20s, was found shortly after 1800 PST.

events.title: Lightning near Greenfield
events.description: 1 death. Kern County. Autospy confirmed Bakersfield man was struck and killed by lightning. The individual was found unresponsive just before 7 PM PDT by a family member.

events.title: Flash Flood near Inwood
events.description: 2 deaths. Shasta County. A 19 year old man and a 19-year-old women were driving in a vehicle that was swept off a small bridge over Lack Creek. Both were found drowned, their car about three quarters of a mile down stream. About 3.12 inches of rain fell nearby, measured by a RAWS station at Shingletown over 24 hours. Of that, 2.87 inches of rain fell in the 5 hours before the accident.

events.title: Flash Flood near Yucca Vly Arpt
events.description: 1 death. San Bernardino County. Severe flooding impacted much of Joshua Tree. Many roads were covered with water, mud, and rocks. Several homes were flooded, including one which was destroyed. A one year old boy was swept away in his back yard before being rescued. One man died when his vehicle was swept down a flooded wash.

events.title: Flash Flood near Adelanto Hlndale Arp
events.description: 1 death. San Bernardino County. CHP reported a flooded wash with multiple cars stuck in the area. 4 inches of rain recorded in gauge within 2 hours on the steep slope of big Mt Baldy. A hiker parked their car in the small town of Mt Baldy and hiked to the top. Hail and lightning caused them to go back down the mountain early. They used the dry creek to go back|down and were swept away in a flash flood over 10 feet, per NWS Storm Survey of high water marks on trees. The hiker's car was found the next|day during the NWS Storm Survey. The car was destroyed and the person drowned somewhere along the middle or bottom of the…

events.title: Lightning near Marina Del Ray
events.description: 1 death. Los Angeles County. An isolated thunderstorm moved across the Venice Beach area along the Los Angeles county coast. Lightning struck the water, injuring 13 people and killing one person.
